title: TS-06 HTTP skeleton: createApp, error mapping, invoke key, /health
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 6 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 6); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Create the Hono application factory that every later route registers into, the error-to-status mapping, the invoke-key and X-Tenant-Id middleware, GET /health, and the structural guard that every route declares its audience.

## Kind
mechanical-port: the Python source below is the specification. Keep its structure, names (camelCase), branches and messages. Do not redesign anything.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/06-http-skeleton-createapp-error-mapping-in origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): hTTP skeleton: createApp, error mapping, invoke key, /health

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/06-http-skeleton-createapp-error-mapping-in
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

## Files to create or change
- `conversation/src/http/app.ts`
- `conversation/src/http/errors.ts`
- `conversation/src/http/route-audience.ts`
- `conversation/features-support/steps/org-path-routing.steps.ts`
- `conversation/test/route-audience.test.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
`createApp(deps: AppDeps): Hono` where `AppDeps = {clock: Clock; ids: IdSource; store: MessagingStore; invokeKey: string | null}`. `statusFor(error: unknown): number` returns the same status as Python `_status_for_error` for each error class (copy the mapping table into a vitest). `class DomainError extends Error {constructor(readonly code: string, message: string)}` and subclasses named exactly as the Python exceptions. Error body is `{"detail": <message>}`. `declareRoute(app, {method, path, audience: "public"|"user"|"operator"|"worker"|"integration"}, handler)` is the only way to register a route; the vitest fails when any registered route lacks an audience. `X-Tenant-Id` header present => 400 `{detail: "X-Tenant-Id is not accepted"}`. Invoke key: when `deps.invokeKey` is non-null every route except `/health` requires header `X-Chatticus-Invoke-Key` equal to it (constant-time compare via `crypto.timingSafeEqual`), else 403.

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Python source to port (keep structure; read it fully before writing)
- `python/src/chatticus/http/app.py lines 561-650 (middleware, invoke key, _status_for_error) and 2128-2175 (health and app assembly)`
Rule: mechanical ports keep the Python file's structure and cite the Python line range in the commit body. Behavior that no scenario encodes is still kept.

## Behavior spec (Gherkin, ported unchanged)
Existing features that must pass under cucumber-js when this ticket closes. Do NOT edit these `.feature` files except where this ticket says a behavior changed.

### features/org_path_routing.feature
Scenarios: Org-scoped routes live under /orgs/{tenant_id}; X-Tenant-Id is rejected at the front door; Another tenant cannot post on the channel via the wrong org path; Health stays outside the org path; Authentication routes stay outside the org path; GET /me stays outside the org path
Step texts to implement in TypeScript (exact step text, then the Python step that implements it today):
```text

tenant "anthus" user "ryan" has a bot named "Researcher"   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:280
the front door receives POST /orgs/anthus/channels for user "ryan" with bots:   <-  features/steps/org_path_routing_steps.py:11
the channel response has tenant_id "anthus"   <-  features/steps/org_path_routing_steps.py:35
the front door receives GET /orgs/anthus/users/ryan/bots with header X-Tenant-Id anthus   <-  features/steps/org_path_routing_steps.py:42
the front door rejects X-Tenant-Id   <-  features/steps/org_path_routing_steps.py:56
tenant "anthus" user "ryan" has opened a channel with bots:   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:338
tenant "other" posts "intrusion" on the channel via org path "other-household"   <-  features/steps/org_path_routing_steps.py:63
posting fails because the tenant does not match   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:795
the channel has 0 messages   <-  features/steps/messaging_steps.py:508
a front door serving named environment "development" with HTTP   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:506
GET /health reports environment "development"   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:514
"/auth/callback" is outside the principal marker system   <-  features/steps/principal_steps.py:77

```
Cucumber expressions: convert each Python `{name}` parse pattern to `{string}`, `{int}` or `{word}` using `npx tsx conversation/bin/convert-step-pattern.ts '<pattern>'` (from ticket 3) and review the output by hand. Step text must not change unless behavior changed. Steps call `this.api` (HTTP via `app.request()`) for HTTP steps and the same domain functions the routes call for direct steps; steps never reach into a store.
Step file(s) to write: under `conversation/features-support/steps/` as named in Files above (at most about 400 lines each; split by subject).

Failing run first (required):
```text
1. Write or port the step file(s) and any new .feature file.
2. cd conversation && npx cucumber-js ../features/<feature>.feature   -> confirm the scenarios FAIL for the right reason (missing production code, not a typo in a step). Save the first failing summary line for the commit body.
3. Write the smallest production code that passes. Re-run until green.
```
Manifest: when EVERY scenario of a feature is covered by this ticket (not marked partial above), add `features/<name>.feature` to `features/ported-features.txt` and add `<name>` to the alternation in `python/behave.ini` `exclude_re` (the manifest vitest `conversation/test/ported-features-manifest.test.ts` fails if they disagree). For a partial feature leave the manifest alone; the ticket named in the note finishes it. To run a partial feature, pass the path and `--name '<scenario>'` to cucumber-js; if CLI paths do not override the config paths, stop and report.

## Dependencies (blocked-by)

```text

```
moto setup (copied from the `conversation` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml):
```text

nohup moto_server -p 5555 > moto.log 2>&1 &
```

If the ticket added a feature to the manifest also run `cd conversation && npx cucumber-js` (full manifest) and `cd python && behave` is NOT required for ported features, but run `cd python && black --check src ../features tests && ruff check src ../features tests` if you touched anything under python/ or features/steps/.
Final cleanup before pushing:
```text
git status
```
Make sure NO `.orig`, `.rej`, `node_modules`, `build/`, `dist/`, `moto.log`, `.venv` or other stray files are staged: `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.orig$|\.rej$|node_modules|(^|/)build/|(^|/)dist/|moto\.log|\.venv'` must print nothing.

## Notes
Hono basics (`new Hono()`, `app.request()`) are stable; do not use streaming here (ticket 5 and 19).

## Stop rules
If anything in this ticket is wrong, ambiguous, impossible, or contradicted by the code you find (a Python line range does not match, a step has no Python match, a library API differs from what is written, a scenario cannot pass without changing its text), STOP and report to the orchestrator with the exact file, line and observation. Never improvise, never weaken or delete a scenario to make it pass, never add a fallback or a compatibility branch.

## Python to delete
No production Python is deleted by this ticket (the one big deletion is ticket 40). The only deletions allowed: the per-feature step file of each feature newly added to the manifest, because the manifest vitest requires it: features/steps/org_path_routing_steps.py (if it exists). Shared step files (control_plane_steps.py, capability_policy_steps.py, messaging_steps.py, organization_steps.py and the like) are never edited here; the last ticket that uses them leaves them for ticket 40.

comments.text: Corrections from the TS-07 prototype (branch ts/07-cognito-verifier, 232def30). Apply to this ticket: (1) the conversation tsconfig has erasableSyntaxOnly, so constructor parameter properties are not allowed; declare fields explicitly. (2) A missing Authorization header is 403 in Python and in the features, not 401. (3) Check org status ENABLED after resolving the principal, as verify_org_access does, because the suspended scenario needs the suspended principal back. (4) The Principal type includes organizationStatus and workerId. (5) test-jwt.ts both mints tokens and holds the injected JWKS. (6) cucumber-js with a single .feature path still runs the whole manifest. (7) aws-jwt-verify 5.2.1 and jose 6.2.12 are pinned exactly: CognitoJwtVerifier.create({userPoolId, tokenUse:'id', clientId}), verifier.cacheJwks(jwks) is synchronous, verifier.verify(token) is async, and an unknown kid triggers a network JWKS refetch, so tests reuse the kid.

right_now_summary: The HTTP skeleton, error mapping, invoke-key checks, tenant rejection, and health route are being implemented.
